items.title: `ablinfer` is pip-installed at module import, unpinned, without user consent

findings.title: `ablinfer` is pip-installed at module import, unpinned, without user consent
findings.explanation: Slicer imports every installed module's script at startup to discover its classes, so this installs a package from PyPI into Slicer's shared Python on first start after installation, for every user, with no prompt, no version pin and no record. It also drags in `docker`/`requests` (imported at lines 18, 33) and can silently upgrade or conflict with packages Slicer bundles. Offline machines fail here and then the module cannot load at all because lines 28-33 import from the package unconditionally.
findings.suggestion: Remove the import-time pip_install; use the Slicer extension build system (install into the extension's own site-packages via CMake/SuperBuild, as the commented block in SuperBuild.cmake:32-36 suggests) or a user-confirmed, version-pinned install button per the ScriptedLoadableModule dependency-install convention.

findings.title: Automatic package installation on module import
findings.explanation: The module automatically attempts to pip install 'ablinfer' upon import if not present. While not PyTorch or a restricted bundle, automatic package installation on module import is discouraged in Slicer extensions because it modifies the shared environment without explicit user confirmation during module usage or setup.
findings.suggestion: Move package installation or check into user-triggered initialization or setup rather than at module import time.

findings.title: Package installed into Slicer's Python environment at module import without consent
findings.explanation: At import of the module (and transitively of IntraSampleRegistration.py, which imports the module), if 'ablinfer' is missing the code runs pip install with no user confirmation. This changes the shared Slicer Python environment for users who never open this module, and ablinfer's own dependencies (possibly including docker/requests versions) are pulled in unchecked.
findings.suggestion: Move the import into the inference code path, ask for user confirmation before pip install, and declare the requirement in a way the user can see.

items.title: Committed model descriptor is a placeholder; no unit tests are registered

findings.title: Committed model descriptor is a placeholder; no unit tests are registered
findings.evidence: you shouldn't see this, this file should be retrieved during build
findings.explanation: The file installed by CMake (CMakeLists.txt:20) is not valid JSON, so any build that does not run the SuperBuild download (offline build, download failure, or a user running from a checkout) produces a module whose inference step fails with 'Unable to load inference model'. Additionally both Testing/Python/CMakeLists.txt files keep the unittest registration commented out, and ABLTemporalBoneSegmentationModule.py defines no test class at all.
findings.suggestion: Commit a valid, versioned model descriptor and add at least a smoke test (module loads, atlas/mask files load) for both modules.

items.title: Local variable 'docker' shadows the docker module in the error handler

findings.title: Local variable 'docker' shadows the docker module in the error handler
findings.evidence:
docker = self.inferDockerHost.text.strip()
            is_docker = True
findings.explanation: In click_infer_apply, 'docker' is assigned as a string in the local branch and is unbound in the remote branch. The except block then evaluates docker.errors.ImageNotFound, which raises AttributeError or UnboundLocalError and hides the real inference error.
findings.suggestion: Rename the local variable (e.g. docker_host) so the module name is not shadowed.

items.title: Model descriptor is downloaded from a mutable branch at build time, without checksum, overwriting a tracked source file

findings.title: Model descriptor is downloaded from a mutable branch at build time, without checksum, overwriting a tracked source file
findings.evidence:
## Pull the latest model JSON file on build
set(_download_model COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND}
findings.explanation: The build step runs urllib.request.urlretrieve against `.../temporal-bone-segmentation/master/ABLTempSeg.json` and writes the result over `${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/ABLTemporalBoneSegmentationModule/Resources/Models/ABLTempSeg.json`. That JSON determines which container image / remote model id is executed on the user's machine, so the content that runs is whatever is on someone else's `master` at build time — not what was reviewed here — and no checksum is checked (unlike the atlas download, which does use SHA256, line 1200-1203). It also writes into the source checkout, which dirties the tree and fails on read-only sources.
findings.suggestion: Commit a real model descriptor and pin it, or download with a versioned URL plus SHA256 verification at runtime into the user's cache directory, not into the source tree.

findings.title: Build downloads model JSON from an unpinned branch at build time
findings.explanation: SuperBuild.cmake fetches ABLTempSeg.json from the master branch of another repository with no checksum and writes it into the source tree. The model configuration used by the module can change without any review of this extension, and the build depends on network access.
findings.suggestion: Pin to a release tag or commit with a SHA256 check, or commit the file.

items.title: TLS certificate verification disabled for remote inference, and server password stored in plain text

findings.title: TLS certificate verification disabled for remote inference, and server password stored in plain text
findings.evidence:
s = requests.Session()
            s.verify = False
            if username:
                s.auth = (username, password)
findings.explanation: When the user chooses 'Run on a remote server?', the session sends the user's CT data (and Basic-Auth credentials, line 936) over a connection whose certificate is never validated, so any network attacker can intercept both. The password is additionally persisted in clear text in the Slicer settings file (`settings.setValue("ablinfer_server_password", password)`, line 938) and re-loaded into the UI at startup (line 363). Line 37 suppresses the urllib3 warning that would otherwise tell the user.
findings.suggestion: Drop `s.verify = False` (offer an explicit, warned-about opt-in if self-signed certs must be supported), do not persist the password (or store it via a keychain), and remove the global `disable_warnings` call.

findings.title: TLS certificate verification disabled while sending credentials and CT data
findings.evidence:
s = requests.Session()
            s.verify = False
            if username:
                s.auth = (username, password)
findings.explanation: For remote inference, requests.Session is created with verify=False and HTTP basic credentials are attached. An attacker on the network path can impersonate the server, capture the username and password, and receive the uploaded patient CT volume. InsecureRequestWarning is also silenced globally.
findings.suggestion: Keep verification enabled by default, use a CA bundle or an explicit opt-in for self-signed servers, and document it.

items.title: logging used without importing the logging module

findings.title: `logging.warning` used without importing logging, so remote model retrieval failure raises NameError
findings.evidence: logging.warning("Encountered an error retrieving model from remote: " + str(e))
findings.explanation: `logging` is never imported in this file. When fetching the model from a remote server fails, the except handler raises NameError instead of degrading gracefully to the locally configured model, and the user sees a confusing traceback.
findings.suggestion: Add `import logging` (or use `slicer.util.errorDisplay`/print as elsewhere in the file).

findings.title: logging used without importing the logging module
findings.evidence:
except Exception as e:
                logging.warning("Encountered an error retrieving model from remote: " + str(e))
findings.explanation: run_inference calls logging.warning when the remote model retrieval fails, but the module never imports logging. The fallback path raises NameError instead of continuing with the local model, so remote inference fails with an unrelated error.
findings.suggestion: Add 'import logging' at the top or use print/slicer logging.

items.title: Declared module dependencies are empty although Elastix is required at import

findings.title: Declared module dependencies are empty although Elastix is required at import
findings.evidence: self.parent.dependencies = []
findings.explanation: The module imports `Elastix` at line 16 and `IntraSampleRegistration.py` imports it at line 4; if SlicerElastix is missing, the module fails to load entirely instead of Slicer warning the user. Same for IntraSampleRegistration.py:87.
findings.suggestion: Set `self.parent.dependencies = ["Elastix"]` (and in the second module) so Slicer reports the missing dependency.

items.title: Elastix logic and mutable UI state created/held at class level

findings.title: Elastix logic and mutable UI state created/held at class level
findings.evidence:
registrationSteps = []
    volumePairs = []
findings.explanation: In IntraSampleRegistration.py these lists and `elastixLogic = Elastix.ElastixLogic()` (line 100) are class attributes, and ABLTemporalBoneSegmentationModule.py:151 instantiates `Elastix.ElastixLogic()` at class definition time (i.e. at import). State therefore leaks between widget instances/reloads and an Elastix logic object is constructed even if the user never opens the module.
findings.suggestion: Initialise these in `__init__`/`setup` as instance attributes.

items.title: Export recursively deletes an existing subfolder of the user-chosen directory

findings.title: Export recursively deletes an existing subfolder of the user-chosen directory
findings.explanation: `export_for_cardinalsim` is called with a directory picked via QFileDialog (line 1038) and unconditionally `shutil.rmtree`s `<directory>/<volumeName>_dicom` if it exists, with no confirmation. If the user selects a non-empty folder (the dialog text asks for an empty one but nothing enforces it) and a folder of that name is already there, its contents are destroyed irreversibly. The name is derived from a user-editable volume name.
findings.suggestion: Refuse to write into a non-empty directory, or ask for confirmation before removing anything, and use a temporary folder plus explicit copy.

findings.title: Existing user folder deleted without confirmation during export
findings.explanation: export_for_cardinalsim calls shutil.rmtree on any existing '<volume>_dicom' folder in the chosen directory. The dialog text asks for an empty folder, but nothing enforces it, so prior exports or user data with that name are silently erased.
findings.suggestion: Ask for confirmation or refuse to overwrite a non-empty directory.

items.title: Export writes to current working directory if the folder dialog is cancelled

findings.title: Export writes to current working directory if the folder dialog is cancelled
findings.evidence:
target = qt.QFileDialog.getExistingDirectory(None, "Choose an output directory *MUST BE EMPTY*")
        ABLTemporalBoneSegmentationModuleLogic.export_for_cardinalsim(self.movingSelector.currentNode(), self.exportSelector.currentNode(), target)
findings.explanation: getExistingDirectory returns an empty string on cancel. The code passes it on without checking, and export_for_cardinalsim calls os.path.abspath('') (the process CWD), so DICOM and label files are written to an arbitrary location the user never chose.
findings.suggestion: Return early if target is empty.

findings.title: Global warning suppression at import
findings.evidence: urllib3.disable_warnings(urllib3.exceptions.InsecureRequestWarning)
findings.explanation: Executed when Slicer imports the module at startup, this silences insecure-request warnings for all of Slicer's Python, hiding the `verify = False` issue from the user and from other code.
findings.suggestion: Remove it; if truly needed, scope suppression to the single request.

items.title: No functional tests and no clinical-use disclaimer

findings.title: No functional tests and no clinical-use disclaimer
findings.explanation: Test directories contain only commented-out ctest lines and IntraSampleRegistrationTest.runTest is an empty placeholder. Users get no automated coverage of the registration or export logic and no statement that output is not for clinical diagnosis.
findings.suggestion: Add a sample-data test and a research-use disclaimer.

items.title: No research/clinical-use disclaimer or model validation information

findings.title: No research/clinical-use disclaimer or model validation information
findings.evidence: This 3D Slicer module handles spacing resampling, fiducial registration, rigid registration, and inference of the major structures of CT temporal bone scans.
findings.explanation: The module produces anatomical segmentations of temporal bone structures used downstream (e.g. CardinalSim), but the README gives no statement that it is for research use, no accuracy/validation figures, and no model provenance beyond a link; the Docker image version actually run depends on the remote model descriptor.
findings.suggestion: Add a research-use disclaimer and cite the network's validation study and image version.

items.title: Option deletes every fiducial node in the scene without confirmation

findings.title: Option deletes every fiducial node in the scene without confirmation
findings.evidence:
def clear_all_markups_from_scene():
        for n in slicer.mrmlScene.GetNodesByClass("vtkMRMLMarkupsFiducialNode"): slicer.mrmlScene.RemoveNode(n)
findings.explanation: Called from `finalize_input` (line 606) whenever the 'Clear All Markups When Loading New Input Volume' checkbox is ticked. It removes all fiducial markups in the scene, including ones the user created for other purposes, with no confirmation and no undo prompt.
findings.suggestion: Only remove markups created by this module (track their node IDs), or ask for confirmation.

items.title: Server password stored in plaintext application settings

findings.title: Server password stored in plaintext application settings
findings.evidence:
settings.setValue("ablinfer_server_username", username) 
                  settings.setValue("ablinfer_server_password", password)
findings.explanation: The password typed into the remote server field is written to Slicer's persistent settings on every run. Any local user or process that can read the settings file obtains the credential in cleartext.
findings.suggestion: Do not persist passwords; store them in the OS keyring or only keep them for the session.

items.title: scm_revision points to a moving branch

findings.title: scm_revision points to a moving branch
findings.evidence: "scm_revision": "master"
findings.explanation: The catalog entry uses scm_revision 'master', so the indexed build can change without a catalog update. The reviewed commit is 227bc565ddec65509bac6dcbbddd6c02e718eaeb, which the entry does not pin.
findings.suggestion: Pin scm_revision to a specific commit or release tag.

items.title: IDE project files are committed despite being git-ignored

findings.title: IDE project files are committed despite being git-ignored
findings.evidence:
# Idea
.idea/
findings.explanation: .idea/ is listed in .gitignore yet 9 .idea files (including a 26 KB .idea/workspace.xml that typically records local paths and usernames) are in the repository; .gitignore also carries leftovers from an unrelated project (SkullThicknessMapping lines 127-130). Harmless but noise.
findings.suggestion: Remove the committed .idea files and the unrelated ignore entries.
